facts.text: Malta earned its name when a Great Northern Railway official spun a globe and landed on the Mediterranean island of Malta.
In 2000, a 77‑million‑year‑old Brachylophosaurus nicknamed Leonardo was unearthed north of Malta, one of only four dinosaurs fossilized.
The Great Plains Dinosaur Museum & Field Station, home to Leonardo, sits beside the historic Phillips County Museum that showcases Native American, cowboy, and pioneer artifacts.
Amtrak’s Empire Builder stops daily at Malta Station, an unmanned depot that opens an hour before and after each train.
The Little Rocky Mountains, just 40 miles south, are steeped in mining and outlaw lore, while Nelson Reservoir to the east offers fishing for walleye and trout.
Malta’s water comes from wells pumped to two tanks on Hillcrest, then treated to meet safety standards before entering the city system.
